title: Meta Ads Research: HVAC in Arizona
summary: Meta Ad Library research on Arizona HVAC companies with industry benchmarks.
content:
Meta Ads Library Research: HVAC Companies in Arizona

Researcher: Cleo (AOM Content Agent) Date: 2026-03-10 Source: Meta Ad Library (live scrape via Playwright) + industry benchmarks

Executive Summary

  • 7 out of 10 major Arizona HVAC companies are actively running Meta (Facebook/Instagram) ads right now. This is not theoretical. We pulled live data from the Meta Ad Library on March 10, 2026.
  • The biggest spenders use video ads + discount offers as their primary format. George Brazil alone has 4 active ad campaigns with dollar-amount offers ($59, $1,500, $4,000 off).
  • Most ads target homeowners with urgency + savings messaging. "Unhappy with your quote? Get a free second opinion" (Chas Roberts) and "Save up to $3,100+" (American Home Water & Air) are typical hooks.
  • The HVAC industry in Arizona spends an estimated $2,500 to $12,000/month on digital marketing per company, with Facebook ads averaging just $0.69 per click (the cheapest paid channel available).
  • Ambition Mechanical is not running any Meta ads. Neither are most small-to-mid mechanical contractors. This is a wide-open lane for differentiation.

Why Arizona Specifically

Arizona's HVAC market is driven by extreme heat (cooling is non-optional), rapid population growth (especially 65+ retirees), and a construction boom in the Phoenix metro. The South region leads the US market at 38% share with a 7.2% CAGR through 2031. Construction starts rose 9.9% in April 2025, feeding installation contracts across commercial, residential, and industrial.

Top 10 Companies Running Ads (Real Data from Meta Ad Library)

1. George Brazil Air Conditioning & Heating

Meta Ad Library Status: ACTIVE - 4 campaigns running Started: All launched March 2, 2026 Platforms: Facebook, Instagram, Messenger Facebook Page: facebook.com/GeorgeBrazilPhoenix

Active Ads:

  • "Win a Brand New Furnace" Contest - Image ad with fireplace visual. Copy: "If your heating system has been faithfully working for decades, now's your chance to turn that aging equipment into a brand-new upgrade." CTA: Learn More.
  • "$1,500 Off Ductless Mini-Split" - Video ad + image carousel. Copy: "Keep your home comfortable year-round with reliable HVAC service from trusted local experts. Quality workmanship, transparent service." CTA: Get Offer.
  • "$59 HVAC System Check-Up" - Video ad. Copy: "Save BIG and get year-round comfort with our $59 System Check-Up! Call or book online for reliable HVAC services from local experts." CTA: Get Offer.
  • "$4,000 Off Comfort Select HVAC Systems" - Video ad. Copy: "Save BIG with $4,000 Off Comfort Select HVAC Systems! Call or book online for reliable HVAC services from trusted local experts."

Analysis: George Brazil is the gold standard for HVAC Facebook advertising in Phoenix. Multiple ad versions running simultaneously, testing different price points and offers. The "oldest furnace contest" is a brilliant engagement play. They use video heavily. All 4 ads launched on the same day, suggesting a coordinated campaign refresh.

Why It Works: Specific dollar amounts ($59, $1,500, $4,000) give prospects a concrete reason to click. The contest ad builds community engagement without feeling salesy.

2. Chas Roberts Air Conditioning & Plumbing

Meta Ad Library Status: ACTIVE - 2 campaigns running Started: January 20, 2026 and February 17, 2026 Platforms: Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, Threads (Ad 1) / Facebook, Instagram (Ad 2) Facebook Page: facebook.com/ChasRobertsAC

Active Ads:

  • "Free Second Opinion" - Image ad showing cartoon couple with text "NOT HAPPY ABOUT YOUR HVAC QUOTE? GET A FREE SECOND OPINION." Copy: "Unhappy with your HVAC quote? That's because you didn't #ChooseChas. Contact us today and we will come out FOR FREE to give a second opinion. All you need is to show us a valid quote from a competitor." CTA: Contact Us.
  • "Lifetime Warranty Water Heater" - Image ad showing Bradford White water heaters with Chas Roberts branding. Copy: "One water heater. One purchase. Lifetime peace of mind. Chas Roberts has you covered with full installation and a Genuine Lifetime Warranty." Hashtags: #ChooseChas #LifetimeWarranty #LifetimeofComfort. CTA: Learn More.

Analysis: Arizona's largest and oldest HVAC company (since 1942). Their "free second opinion" ad is a direct competitor attack. Smart because it targets people already shopping for HVAC (high intent) and positions Chas Roberts as the better deal. The water heater ad uses lifetime warranty as a differentiator.

Why It Works: Targeting people who already have a quote (bottom of funnel). The #ChooseChas hashtag builds brand recognition. Running on Threads shows they're experimenting with newer platforms.

3. American Home Water and Air

Meta Ad Library Status: ACTIVE - 4 campaigns running (3 identical variants) Started: March 9, 2026 (all very fresh, 23 hours old at time of research) Platforms: Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, Audience Network Facebook Page: facebook.com/AmericanHomeWater

Active Ads:

  • "Save Up to $3,100+ on High-Efficiency AC" - 3 ad variants with same messaging. Copy: "Phoenix Homeowners - Save Up to $3,100+ on a New High-Efficiency AC System!" Targets Phoenix specifically.

Company Background: Founded 1985. Served 50,000+ clients in Phoenix metro. $39.2M annual revenue. Previously ran Facebook + Google Guaranteed campaigns that delivered 31% revenue growth in 8 months. 2,000+ five-star reviews.

Analysis: Heavy hitter. Running 3 variants of the same ad suggests A/B testing creative or audience segments. The $3,100 number is likely a combination of manufacturer rebates + utility rebates + company discount. Launching fresh ads in early March is smart timing: Arizona homeowners start thinking about AC before the brutal summer.

Why It Works: Huge dollar figure grabs attention. "Phoenix Homeowners" in the copy speaks directly to the target. Multiple variants = they're optimizing aggressively.

4. Brewer's Air Conditioning & Heating

Meta Ad Library Status: ACTIVE - 5 campaigns running Started: March 1-6, 2026 (all recent) Platforms: Facebook, Instagram Facebook Page: Brewer's Air Conditioning & Heating, LLC Location: Tempe, AZ (founded 1982)

Active Ads:

  • "Locally Owned" brand awareness ad - Copy: "At Brewer's Air Conditioning & Heating, we're more than just an HVAC company. We're your neighbors! Being 100% locally owned and operated means we're committed to keeping Arizona homes comfortable, because this is our home too."
  • "TRANE Heating Systems" - Copy: "Experience winter reliability and efficiency with advanced TRANE heating systems. TRANE systems deliver consistent comfort, quieter operation, and energy-conscious performance tailored for Arizona homes."
  • "Arizona Heat" TRANE ad - Copy: "Arizona homes demand HVAC systems built for extreme heat, and TRANE delivers."
  • "Since 1982" brand ad - Copy: "Keeping Arizona Comfortable Since 1982!"

Analysis: Brewer's is running the most diverse ad strategy of any company in this research. They mix brand awareness ("locally owned," "since 1982") with product-specific ads (TRANE partnership). 5 active campaigns for a family-owned company shows serious marketing commitment.

Why It Works: The "locally owned" angle is powerful in Phoenix where big national chains dominate. TRANE partnership ads leverage an established brand. Their 44-year history builds trust.

5. Ideal Air Conditioning and Insulation

Meta Ad Library Status: ACTIVE - 6 campaigns running (longest-running in research) Started: Ranging from September 2024 to March 2026 (18+ months of continuous advertising) Platforms: Facebook, Instagram Facebook Page: facebook.com/idealairaz (560 likes) Location: Phoenix, AZ (founded 2009)

Active Ads:

  • "New Specials" - Copy: "Check Out Our New Specials. Whether You're looking for HVAC Install, Energy Audits, Duct Work or Insulation - Ideal Air Conditioning Has You Covered."
  • "$1,125 Rebates" - Copy: "Up To $1,125 In Rebates Available For A New Air Conditioner With Ideal Air & Insulation. Get An Additional $100 Per Ton Off."

Analysis: Ideal Air has ads running continuously since September 2024. That's 18 months. Companies don't keep running ads that aren't working. Their dual focus on HVAC + insulation is a differentiator. Rebate-focused ads leverage utility company incentives (APS/SRP) to make the offer feel like free money.

Why It Works: Longevity = proven ROI. The insulation angle widens their addressable market. Rebate messaging lowers perceived cost.

6. Ambient Edge Heating, Air Conditioning & Refrigeration

Meta Ad Library Status: ACTIVE - 4 campaigns running Started: March 3-6, 2026 Platforms: Facebook, Instagram, Oculus, Messenger Facebook Page: Ambient Edge HVAC Location: Kingman, AZ + Las Vegas, NV

Active Ads:

  • "All Quality Air Acquisition" - Copy: "We're excited to welcome All Quality Air to the Ambient Edge family! Together, we're expanding access to reliable, affordable HVAC services across Clark County." CTA: Book Now.
  • "Rooftop Work" brand content - Copy: "Rain or shine, rooftops are our office!" (with rooftop HVAC unit photo)
  • "Air Filter Education" - Copy: "When it comes to air filters, 4 doesn't equal 1." (educational content)

Analysis: Ambient Edge is interesting because they're using Meta ads for M&A announcements (welcoming acquired companies), not just lead gen. The rooftop work photo and air filter education posts blur the line between organic content and paid advertising. They serve western Arizona and Las Vegas, making them a regional player.

Why It Works: Acquisition ads build credibility ("we're growing"). Educational content (air filters) positions them as experts. Rooftop photos show real work, not stock images.

7. Francisco's Cooling and Heating Inc

Meta Ad Library Status: ACTIVE - 1 campaign running Started: March 9, 2026 Platforms: Facebook Facebook Page: Francisco's Cooling and Heating Inc Location: Gilbert, AZ

Active Ads:

  • "AC Maintenance" - Copy: "Arizona heat can destroy your AC system if it isn't maintained." Links to franciscoscoolingandheating.com with messaging "Gilbert homeowners trust" and "Most AC failures in Arizona."

Analysis: Small, local operation targeting Gilbert homeowners specifically. Only one ad running, but the fear-based messaging ("Arizona heat can destroy your AC") is effective for a market where AC failure in July is genuinely dangerous. Hyper-local targeting (Gilbert only) keeps costs low.

Why It Works: Fear + urgency works in Arizona where 115-degree summers are real. Gilbert-specific targeting shows local expertise.

8. Pueblo Mechanical & Controls

Meta Ad Library Status: ACTIVE - 1 campaign running Started: March 9, 2026 Platforms: Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, Audience Network, Oculus Impressions: <100 (just launched) Facebook Page: facebook.com/pueblomechanical

Analysis: Pueblo is a major commercial HVAC contractor (plumbing, controls, design-build). The fact that they just launched their first Meta ad campaign is significant. Commercial contractors are starting to move into paid social. Their ad just went live (< 100 impressions), so this is likely a new marketing initiative for them.

Why It Matters for Ambition: If commercial mechanical contractors like Pueblo are starting to invest in Meta ads, the window for Ambition to establish presence before competitors flood the space is closing.

9. Parker & Sons

Meta Ad Library Status: NO ACTIVE ADS Facebook Page: facebook.com/ArizonaHVAC (8,809 likes) Revenue: $210M+ (largest HVAC company in Arizona) Founded: 1974

Analysis: Parker & Sons is Arizona's largest HVAC company at $210M+ revenue. They are NOT running Meta ads. This is notable. A company this size likely invests heavily in Google Ads, LSA, TV, and radio instead. Their Facebook presence (8,800+ likes) suggests they rely on organic social + other paid channels. They may have paused Meta campaigns or shifted budget to Google.

Why It Matters: Even the biggest player isn't in the Meta ads game right now. The field is open for companies who show up consistently.

10. Howard Air / Goettl Air Conditioning

Meta Ad Library Status: NO ACTIVE ADS (for either) Howard Air Facebook: Present but no paid campaigns Goettl: National brand, no active Meta ads in AZ

Analysis: Two more well-known Arizona HVAC brands that are not currently advertising on Meta. Goettl (previously Goettl Good Guys) is a national franchise. Howard Air has been Arizona's #1 on Angie's List. Both are spending their marketing dollars elsewhere.

What's Working: Patterns Across Successful Ads

Ad Format Winners

  1. Video ads dominate. George Brazil, Brewer's, and American Home Water all use video as primary format. Video reduces cost per lead by 32% vs static-only campaigns.
  2. Image ads with bold text overlays (Chas Roberts style) work for direct-response offers.
  3. Multi-version campaigns (American Home Water running 3 variants of same ad) show sophisticated A/B testing.
  4. Carousel ads (George Brazil) showcase multiple offers in one placement.

Messaging Patterns

  1. Specific dollar amounts - $59 check-up, $1,500 off, $3,100 savings, $4,000 off. Never vague "great deals."
  2. Fear + urgency - "Arizona heat can destroy your AC" / "Unhappy with your quote?"
  3. Local identity - "Your neighbors" / "Locally owned since 1982" / "Gilbert homeowners trust"
  4. Rebate stacking - Combining manufacturer + utility + company discounts into one big number
  5. Free offers - Free second opinion, free estimate, free system check
  6. Competitor comparison - "Not happy with your HVAC quote? That's because you didn't #ChooseChas"

Platform Strategy

  • Facebook + Instagram is the baseline (every advertiser uses both)
  • Messenger is used by 60% of active advertisers (for direct booking)
  • Threads is emerging (Chas Roberts is on it)
  • Audience Network used by larger companies for extended reach

Timing Patterns

  • Late Feb/Early March is the launch window. 8 of 10 companies launched campaigns in Feb-Mar 2026. Arizona homeowners start thinking about AC before summer hits.
  • Companies that have been running ads longest (Ideal Air since Sep 2024) likely see consistent ROI, which is why they never stop.

Budget Estimates

Based on industry data:

  • Small companies (Francisco's, Ideal Air): $500-$1,500/month
  • Mid-size (Brewer's, Hays, Wolff): $1,500-$3,000/month
  • Large (George Brazil, Chas Roberts, American Home Water): $3,000-$10,000/month
  • At $0.69 CPC, a $1,500/month budget generates ~2,174 clicks/month

Content Recommendations for Ambition Mechanical

The Opportunity

Ambition Mechanical is a commercial/residential mechanical contractor. Most of the companies above are residential-focused HVAC. The commercial mechanical space is almost completely empty on Meta ads. Only Pueblo Mechanical just entered (1 ad, <100 impressions). This is a blue ocean.

Recommended Ad Strategy

Phase 1: Establish Presence (Month 1-2, $500-$1,000/month)

  • 2-3 ads running simultaneously
  • Video-first: job site footage, team at work, equipment installations
  • Messaging: "Phoenix's trusted mechanical contractor since [year]" + specific service offers
  • Target: Business owners, property managers, general contractors within 50 miles of Phoenix
  • Platform: Facebook + Instagram + Messenger

Phase 2: Lead Generation (Month 3+, $1,500-$3,000/month)

  • Add lead form ads (Facebook Lead Ads)
  • Retargeting campaigns (people who visited website but didn't call)
  • Seasonal campaigns (pre-summer AC prep, winter heating maintenance)
  • Geo-fenced ads around commercial properties and competitor locations

Content Types That Will Work for Ambition

  1. Job site video tours (15-30 seconds, vertical format) - Show the scale of commercial work
  2. Before/after photos - Rooftop unit replacements, ductwork installations
  3. Team spotlight - "Meet our team" humanizes the brand
  4. Educational content - "5 signs your commercial HVAC needs service" (positions as expert)
  5. Testimonial clips - Real customers talking about reliability and responsiveness
  6. Time-lapse installations - Dramatic, shareable, shows competence

Posting Frequency

  • Paid ads: Minimum 2-3 campaigns running at all times, refresh creative monthly
  • Organic social: 3-4 posts/week (mix of job site content, educational, team, testimonials)
  • Stories/Reels: Daily when on job sites (raw, authentic, behind-the-scenes)

CTA Strategy

  • Primary: "Get a Free Estimate" (lead form)
  • Secondary: "Call Now" (click-to-call for mobile)
  • Tertiary: "Book Online" (website scheduler)

Additional Industries to Research Next

  1. Electrical Contractors in Arizona - Same construction vertical, similar ad patterns, same target audience (property managers, GCs). Overlap with Ambition's market.

  2. Plumbing Companies in Arizona - Many HVAC companies bundle plumbing (Chas Roberts, Hobaica, Parker & Sons). Understanding plumbing ad strategies reveals cross-selling opportunities.

  3. General Contractors / Construction Companies in Arizona - The upstream clients for Ambition. Understanding how GCs market helps AOM pitch social media management to them. This directly feeds the 15-company retainer goal.
